title: The Czech June decision raises the full corridor by 25 basis points
summary: On June 18 the Bank Board announced a quarter-percentage-point increase in its two-week repo rate to 3.75%. The discount rate rose to 2.75% and the Lombard rate to 4.75%, also by 25 basis points. The three rates therefore moved in parallel, preserving a corridor two percentage points wide.

The notice specified June 19 as the date when the new levels came into effect. June 18 identifies the public announcement for an event study; June 19 identifies the operational change in a daily policy-rate series. The 25-basis-point increase measures the Board’s action. Its unexpected component and any realized response in the koruna or bond yields require additional pre- and post-release observations.

questions.question: What proportion of the 25-basis-point increase had markets priced?
questions.detail: Compare contracts immediately before 14:30 on June 18 with the 3.75% effective rate and with the change in contract pricing after release.

questions.question: Did short-term market implementation align with the June 19 value date?
questions.detail: Check dated overnight and repo observations on the two days, preserving transaction versus settlement dates and the distinction between market and administered rates.

questions.question: Did markets revise only the current setting or also later expectations?
questions.detail: Compare short and forward rates inside the announcement-only interval, then start a new window when the press conference begins at 15:00.
